title: Next Greater Element
statement:
For every element of an array, find the first element to its **right** that is **strictly greater** than it, and report that element's **value**. If no such element exists, report `-1` for that position.

Equal values do not count as greater. The last element always gets `-1`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `a[0] ... a[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print `n` space-separated integers: the next greater value for each position, in order.

examples.explanation: 6 and 2 both look right and first meet 9. Nothing after 9 is bigger. Each 3 first sees 8 (the other 3 is equal, so it does not count). 8 is last, so -1.
The array is decreasing, so no element has a larger one to its right.
In an increasing array each element's right neighbour is its next greater element.

hints: The brute force scans right from every index, which is O(n^2) in the worst case.
Process the array left to right and keep a stack of indices whose next greater element has not been found yet.

When the current element is larger than the value at the top of the stack, it is the answer for that index: pop and record it, repeat, then push the current index. Each index is pushed and popped once.
